clue.text: Enjoy oneself in routine

definitions.meaning: to get into the swing of things and enjoy the music or a good time
a fixed habit or rut you fall into

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: one is slang for having a good time, the other a settled rut or habit.

clue.text: Cheap fare that's taken after Ash Wednesday?

definitions.text: Cheap fare that's taken after Ash Wednesday?

parts.words: Cheap fare that's taken after Ash Wednesday?
parts.note: Ash Wednesday begins Lent, a period of abstinence, so food eaten then is food of a fast; the plain sense is burgers and chips

explanation.surface: A question about what cheap food people eat once Ash Wednesday has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ash Wednesday opens Lent, when Christians traditionally fast, so the punning reading is food for a fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Burgers and chips served quickly and cheaply are the quick-service meals this phrase names.

clue.text: Form rules on one tile

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket
one is the Roman numeral I
a slate is a roofing tile

explanation.surface: Someone lays down regulations about a single tile.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so 'on' gives LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, a synonym for forming rules.

clue.text: Fancy mother carrying on!

indicators.note: a parent carrying something holds it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dam is a mother animal, as in horse breeding
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that mother keeps on going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts RE (about, on) inside DAM, a mother of livestock. 'carrying on' looks like one phrase meaning misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a daydream or flight of imagination, and as a verb both mean imagine.

clue.text: Make-up nearly everyone needed for walk

parts.note: a person's make-up is their constitution

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: everyone means all

explanation.surface: Cosmetics that almost everybody wants before going for a stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ALL (everyone) to AL. 'Make-up' looks like cosmetics but means physical composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A constitutional is a short walk taken for the sake of one's health.

clue.text: Brown timber planed at the front

indicators.note: planing shaves wood off, here only the first letter is shaved away

parts.note: lumber is sawn timber, the usual American word

explanation.surface: A carpenter's note about brown wood smoothed at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timber' must first become LUMBER; 'planed at the front' then removes its L. Trimming TIMBER itself gets nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is an earthy brown pigment and the colour named after it.

clue.text: Mineral derivative of serotonin

indicators.note: something derived is made from the material of another, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A chemistry claim that some mineral is derived from the brain chemical serotonin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derivative of' reshuffles the nine letters of SEROTONIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironstone is a sedimentary rock rich in iron ore, a mineral deposit.

clue.text: Is reversing with pleasure fitting for a car?

indicators.note: reversing turns the little word is back to front

parts.note: delight means pleasure

explanation.surface: A question about whether a reversing car with something enjoyable fitted is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' makes SI from 'Is'; the motoring words suggest a car backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp fitted at the front of a car, a piece of its equipment.

clue.text: Joints I served with fish

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A diner is served the joints of meat alongside fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served with' simply joins the pieces; the fish comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpi are the wrist bones, so the plural names the wrist joints.

clue.text: Slowly, minute by minute?

parts.note: minute, meaning tiny, is little
minute again means little

explanation.surface: Progress described as going slowly, one minute at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' looks like a unit of time but is read as tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradually and slowly are both expressed by this idiom of steady progress.

clue.text: Music group appearing in concert, etc, often with backing

indicators.note: with backing says the hidden letters are read backwards
something appearing in the words is contained within them, so the letters are found inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A band turns up at concerts and similar events, frequently with backing musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'appearing' in the definition, but 'appearing in' is the signal for letters lying inside 'concert, etc, often'; 'with backing' then reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is an ensemble of eight musicians, a kind of music group.

clue.text: Drink lager mixed with European beverage

parts.note: gin is an alcoholic beverage

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A recipe: lager stirred into some continental drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges LAGER plus E into GERALE, which follows GIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger ale is a fizzy soft drink flavoured with ginger.

clue.text: Steering mechanism I dropped over

parts.note: a fin steers a boat, surfboard or rocket
shed means dropped, as leaves are shed

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone let go of the steering gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'over' as part of 'dropped over', but it is the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it has ended, which is a synonym of complete.

clue.text: Coin occupying hole

parts.note: occupying a place means being in it
a vent is an opening or hole

explanation.surface: A coin is lodged in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coin' is a verb here: to coin a word is to make it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a phrase is to create it, so the verb means devise or create.

clue.text: Sandwich, say, as part of a meal to whip up firstly

indicators.note: firstly tells us this piece goes at the start, ahead of the meal part
in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to flog is to whip
a course is one part of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone whips up a sandwich as one part of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich in Kent is home to Royal St George's, a famous links where the Open is played. 'up' reverses FLOG; 'firstly' puts it before COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Sandwich in Kent hosts a championship links, so it is an example of a place to play eighteen holes.

clue.text: Vital thing that's stopped?

parts.note: it reads as a heart or lung that has ceased working, but the instrument in a church has stops, knobs that select its pipes

explanation.walkthrough: The word names both a vital body part and a church instrument whose ranks of pipes are controlled by stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart is a vital body part, and the pipe instrument in churches is fitted with stops.

clue.text: Tourist's sun shield protecting it

indicators.note: a shield protecting something wraps round it, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a visor shields the eyes from the sun
taken as written

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's sun hat keeps something covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' puts IT inside VISOR; the 's of 'Tourist's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist is someone travelling to see a place, which is a synonym for a caller or guest.

clue.text: Bitter winter frost ends, sharp

parts.note: bitter is a type of British ale

indicators.note: ends means the final letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: Bitter winter frost finishing up sharply.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a hoppy British beer, a kind of ale. 'ends' takes R and T, the last letters of 'winter' and 'frost'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp in the sense of quick-witted and watchful is synonymous with being on guard.

clue.text: Wind outside as dry as dust

indicators.note: to wind something is to twist and turn it, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Dry air blowing outside, as dusty as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a breeze but is the verb (rhymes with 'kind'), twisting the letters of OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry as dust describes something dull and boring.

clue.text: Close to Waterloo, heading for Piccadilly, queens squeezing past someone at Covent Garden?

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
the heading of a word is its first letter
two pieces squeezing a third press round it, so it sits inside them

parts.note: ER is the abbreviation for a queen, so two queens give it twice
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A London journey from Waterloo to Piccadilly, squeezing past royalty to reach Covent Garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is home to the Royal Opera House. ER (Elizabeth Regina) is a queen; 'squeezing' puts AGO between the two ERs.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden is London's opera house district, so a person there might be a regular attendee at performances.

clue.text: Cut ace in trial

indicators.note: cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a demon at something is an ace, an expert

explanation.surface: Removing an ace card during a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims DEMON, as in 'a demon at tennis', to its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a trial demonstration or test version of a product.

clue.text: Piece of history, object beyond the horizon?

parts.note: beyond the horizon is far away
an object is a thing

explanation.surface: A historical artefact out on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny, withdrawn in 1961. 'Piece' is a coin, not a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: An old quarter-penny coin, no longer used, is literally a piece of money from the past.

clue.text: Change in Nevada arising with sprinkling of trees in very dry region

indicators.note: in a down clue arising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: dimes are American coins, small change in a US state

indicators.note: a sprinkling scatters things about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Climate change in Nevada brings a scattering of trees to an arid area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arising' reverses DIMES to SEMID; 'sprinkling of' rearranges TREES as ESERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A semidesert is an arid area with slightly more rain than true desert.

clue.text: China beyond corrupt in game

indicators.note: beyond means this piece comes after the other

parts.note: bad means corrupt or rotten
Minton is a famous make of English porcelain china

explanation.surface: Corruption in a sporting event involving China.
explanation.walkthrough: Minton is a Staffordshire pottery firm, so its name stands for china. 'China' looks like the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock, so it is a game.

clue.text: Distant? That's blooming deceptive

parts.note: flowers that are blooming are out
lying means deceptive

explanation.surface: A remark that something flowering far away is misleading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' could be a mild British curse, but here flowers are out.
explanation.definitionFit: Outlying places are remote, far from the centre, so the word means distant.

clue.text: Tales about small child not bad at all, say?

indicators.note: tales placed about a child go round it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: lies are tall tales
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Stories told around a little kid aren't half bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TOT inside LIES. The definition is an example: 'not bad' for 'good' is understatement by negating the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Understatement made by denying the opposite is the figure of speech, and 'not bad at all' is an example.

clue.text: National character of Greece put on tip

indicators.note: in a down clue put on means this piece sits above the next

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
to tip is to lean

explanation.surface: A Greek character is told to tip over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National' is a noun here: a citizen of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Chile, a South American country, is a citizen of that nation.

clue.text: Dog with shaven head, might one be bald?

indicators.note: a shaven head loses its top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog with a shaved head asks if it might end up bald.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with shaven head' drops the B of BEAGLE. The bald one is the North American bird of prey.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald variety is the national bird of the USA, so the bird of prey can be described as bald.

clue.text: Locate a hint

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount or suggestion of something

explanation.definitionFit: To find someone is to track them, and a small hint is a faint suggestion of something.

clue.text: Bolt to run smoothly when lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue being lifted means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to flow is to run smoothly

explanation.surface: A bolt runs smoothly once it is raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a fastening but means to gobble food down.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt food is to gulp it greedily, a synonym of gobble.
